quote: The primordium of the paramesonephric duct is beginning to appear as an invagination of thickened coelomic epithelium over the mesonephros.
note: Supports moving the start bound from CS15 to CS16. CS17 adds that the ducts 'may appear at the previous stage', i.e. CS16, so CS16 is the earliest the source will name.

quote: The most advanced embryos with regard to endodermal spread are also more advanced in other respects. (Nos. 5960 and 7545 already show a neural groove.) It may be that this endoderm is derived from the caudal part of the primitive streak (fig. 6-2).
note: Supports moving the start bound from CS9 to CS8: two stage-8 specimens already show a neural groove. The CS9 summary then treats the groove as established ('Now that the neural groove and the first somites are present').

quote: The remaining wall is made up of the undifferentiated ependymal zone, except for a beginning mantle zone in the region that is to form the ventral horn of gray matter.
note: Supports moving the start bound from CS14 to CS13: a beginning mantle zone is described at CS13, and at CS11 the source says one cannot yet mark off ependymal and mantle zones.

quote: Neurofibrils begin to form for the first time in the rhombencephalic wall, and in most embryos a marginal layer begins to develop.
note: Supports moving the start bound from CS15 to CS12, a three-stage correction. This is the source's first statement that a marginal layer develops.

quote: The remaining wall is made up of the undifferentiated ependymal zone, except for a beginning mantle zone in the region that is to form the ventral horn of gray matter.
note: Supports moving the start bound from CS12 to CS13. At CS11 the source says 'one cannot yet mark off ependymal and mantle' zones; this CS13 sentence names the ependymal zone. O'Rahilly writes ependymal where Uberon says ventricular layer.

quote: Although frequently referred to as the notochord, the axial cells caudal to the prechordal plate are still merely notochordal plate at this stage.
note: Supports moving the END bound from CS9 to CS11. The table had the notochordal plate gone by CS9, but the source still calls the axial cells 'merely notochordal plate' at CS10 and heads a CS11 section 'Notochordal plate and notochord'.

quote: External: lens vesicles are closed; nasal pits are appearing; hand plates are forming.
note: Supports moving the start bound from CS14 to CS15: the CS15 summary is where nasal pits first appear. At CS14 the source says the nasal plate 'is usually flat ... although it has not yet acquired a distinct lip'.

quote: The nasal discs become thicker and form a portion of the ectodermal ring on both sides of the closed neuropore (O'Rahilly and Müller, 1985).
note: Supports moving the start bound from CS13 to CS12. Reachable only via SYNONYMS.tsv: the source states 'the term placode is avoided' and writes nasal disc or nasal plate throughout.
